tools.description:
Create a real AANet workspace with a prepaid USDC balance — the entry
    point for an orchestrator agent starting a new swarm task. Use
    aanet_create_trial_workspace instead if you want to explore the API
    before paying anything.

tools.name: aanet_create_trial_workspace
tools.description:
Create a free trial workspace — no payment, no arguments, works
    immediately. Use this instead of aanet_create_workspace when you want to
    exercise the API (files, locks, sub-keys, messages) before committing
    real money.

    Pre-funded with a small fixed balance (currently 1000 units = $0

tools.name: aanet_get_workspace
tools.description:
Check a workspace's current balance and status — the read-only
    counterpart to every other workspace tool. Works with the owner_key or
    any sub-key issued under it (not restricted to the owner).

    Returns deposit_balance and total_spent in raw integer units ($0.00001
    each), plus is_tria

tools.name: aanet_delete_workspace
tools.description:
Permanently and irreversibly delete a workspace: every sub-key, all
    files, the activity log, and any registered webhooks are destroyed
    along with it — there is no undo and no trash/recycle bin. Requires the
    owner_key; a sub-key gets a 403.

tools.name: aanet_deposit
tools.description:
Fund a real workspace via the x402 protocol — a two-step call using
    the same tool both times. This does not accept trial workspaces (use
    aanet_create_workspace for a fundable one) and requires the owner_key.

    Step 1 — call with only api_key/workspace_id/amount_usd: returns an x402

tools.name: aanet_mint_subkey
tools.description:
Issue a new scoped credential for one sub-agent — the standard way to
    bring a sub-agent into an existing workspace. Requires the owner_key; a
    sub-key cannot mint another sub-key.

    Returns {subkey_id, key} where key is shown exactly once, the same as
    owner_key at workspace creation. G

tools.name: aanet_list_subkeys
tools.description:
List every sub-key ever issued under a workspace (including revoked
    ones), with each one's scope, budget_cap, and spent_so_far — the
    inventory view that complements aanet_get_activity's per-event log.
    Owner_key required; raw key values are never included since they're
    only ever shown

tools.name: aanet_update_subkey
tools.description:
Change a live sub-key's scope and/or budget cap without revoking and
    reissuing it — use this instead of aanet_revoke_subkey + aanet_mint_subkey
    when the sub-agent's credentials themselves should keep working (e.g.
    widening its file scope mid-task, or raising a budget cap it hit).
    Own

    the workspace. Owner_key required.

tools.name: aanet_read_file
tools.description:
Read a file's content, or list a directory's entries if path points
    to one — the read counterpart to aanet_write_file/aanet_append_file.
    Metered per call regardless of file size. Returns {path, content,

tools.name: aanet_acquire_lock
tools.description:
Claim exclusive ownership of a named unit of work so no other
    sub-agent starts the same thing — call this before starting work, not
    after. Returns {lease_expires_at} on success, or a 409 if another
    sub-agent already holds an unexpired lease on the same name (that
    conflict is free — y

tools.name: aanet_renew_lock
tools.description:
Extend a lock you currently hold, before its lease runs out — call
    this instead of aanet_acquire_lock again while work is still in
    progress. Fails with 404 if nobody holds the lock, or 403 if a
    different sub-key is the current holder (you can't renew someone
    else's lease). Returns {l

tools.name: aanet_release_lock
tools.description:
Voluntarily give up a lock you hold, immediately, instead of waiting
    for its lease to expire — always call this as soon as you're done with
    the unit of work, so a sub-agent waiting on it doesn't idle
    unnecessarily. Free (no charge), unlike acquire/renew. Fails with 404 if
    nobody hold

tools.name: aanet_get_activity
tools.description:
Read the server-side audit log of every attempt in this workspace,
    successful or rejected — the authoritative source of what each
    sub-agent actually did, since sub-agents can't fake or skip this the
    way they could misreport their own actions. Owner_key required.

tools.name: aanet_submit_feedback
tools.description:
Report a bug, request a feature, or flag that pricing feels wrong —
    this is the one feedback channel into how the operator prioritizes what
    to build next, not a support ticket that gets a reply. Any valid,
    unrevoked key can call this, owner or sub-key. Returns
    {feedback_id, status} w

tools.name: aanet_request_refund
tools.description:
Ask for a workspace's entire remaining balance back, when its task is
    done and money is left over — call this before aanet_delete_workspace,
    not after. Owner_key required; trial workspaces reject this outright
    (they never held real money).

    This reserves (zeros out) the full balance

tools.name: aanet_get_refund_status
tools.description:
Check the status of every refund request ever made for a workspace —

tools.description:
Register a push endpoint so this workspace calls you instead of you
    calling aanet_get_activity/aanet_get_messages/aanet_acquire_lock in a

    Owner_key required; up to 5 active webhooks per workspace.

tools.description:
List webhooks registered on a workspace — url, subscribed events, and

tools.name: aanet_delete_webhook
tools.description:
Permanently remove a registered webhook — no further events will be
    delivered to it, active or auto-disabled. Owner_key required. There is
    no way to temporarily pause one; delete and re-register with

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: aanet_submit_feedback, aanet_get_messages, aanet_list_webhooks · Private data: aanet_create_trial_workspace, aanet_delete_workspace, aanet_deposit, aanet_mint_subkey, aanet_update_subkey, aanet_revoke_subkey, aanet_read_file, aanet_write_file, aanet_append_file, aanet_delete_file, aanet_send_message, aanet_register_webhook, aanet_list_webhooks, aanet_delete_webhook · Public sink: aanet_write_file, aanet_append_file, aanet_delete_file, aanet_release_lock, aanet_submit_feedback, aanet_send_message, aanet_get_messages, aanet_register_webhook, aanet_delete_webhook, aanet_get_webhook_deliveries · Destructive: aanet_delete_workspace, aanet_write_file, aanet_delete_file, aanet_delete_webhook.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: aanet_submit_feedback, aanet_get_messages, aanet_list_webhooks · Private data: aanet_create_trial_workspace, aanet_delete_workspace, aanet_deposit, aanet_mint_subkey, aanet_update_subkey, aanet_revoke_subkey, aanet_read_file, aanet_write_file, aanet_append_file, aanet_delete_file, aanet_send_message, aanet_register_webhook, aanet_list_webhooks, aanet_delete_webhook · Public sink: aanet_write_file, aanet_append_file, aanet_delete_file, aanet_release_lock, aanet_submit_feedback, aanet_send_message, aanet_get_messages, aanet_register_webhook, aanet_delete_webhook, aanet_get_webhook_deliveries · Destructive: aanet_delete_workspace, aanet_write_file, aanet_delete_file, aanet_delete_webhook

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
